clue.text: Trader disposed to imbibe alcohol

annotationWithheld.why: Trader disposed to imbibe alcohol (3,6): ARTDEALER is TRADER rearranged around ALE, so 'Trader' must be both the definition and the anagram fodder; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Arab MO is cooking divine food

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters of the words before it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An Arab medical officer prepares a heavenly meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cooking' rearranges ARAB, MO and IS together; the 'is' belongs to the fodder as well as the verb in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the food of the gods, so it is food fit for deities.

clue.text: Valentine certainly needs nothing

parts.note: true, as in 'true!' agreeing, means certainly
love is nothing, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A Valentine card certainly needs nothing more to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A Valentine is a sweetheart, the one person you hold dear above all.

clue.text: Provided it's right in the finish

indicators.note: in puts the piece for 'it's right' inside the word for finish

parts.note: the end is the finish
what is due to you is yours by right

explanation.surface: Someone says they supplied what was rightfully owed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places DUE (what is owed by right) inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Endued means endowed or furnished, that is, supplied with a quality.

clue.text: A bit of bacon with fat attached

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
on can mean attached, as a lid is on a jar

explanation.surface: A piece of bacon comes with its fat still on.
explanation.definitionFit: A lardon is a small strip or cube of bacon or pork fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Sentimental Italian capitalist gets the twitch

parts.note: someone from Rome, Italy's capital city, is a Roman
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A soppy Italian financier develops a nervous twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' looks like a money man, but here it means a resident of the capital, Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes someone given to tender, idealised feeling, i.e. soppy or mushy.

clue.text: Decline to employ a medic with no work

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
O, the zero, stands for no or nothing
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Refusing to take on a doctor who is out of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refusal, but it is the definition in its sense of sag or fall away.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or flag, a falling away in vigour.

clue.text: Lawyer thanks HQ for computer files

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
ta is informal British for thanks
a base is a headquarters, as for an army

explanation.surface: A solicitor thanks head office for sending some digital records.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is a structured collection of records stored on a computer.

clue.text: Thawing out in the typing room

definitions.text: Thawing out in the typing room

parts.words: Thawing out in the typing room
parts.note: something no longer frozen could be described as off the ice, and split that way the phrase names a room where typists work

explanation.surface: A clerk warms up in a chilly typing pool.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, 'off ice', for the thawing sense; whole it is a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A typing pool is a workroom for clerical staff, a kind of business room.

clue.text: Reasonably attractive

explanation.surface: Something is fairly good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb it means fairly or moderately; as an adjective it means good-looking or lovely.

clue.text: Reprobate with a spring in his step

definitions.text: with a spring in his step

explanation.surface: A rogue walks with a jaunty bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad or scoundrel is called this; literally it also describes one who leaps along energetically.

clue.text: Mad, mad artist!

indicators.note: mad means crazy or disordered, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a crazy painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Mad' is the anagram signal; the second is part of the fodder with ARTIST. The whole clue hints that a playwright is a wild sort of creator.
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright is a writer of plays, an artist of the stage.

clue.text: Mount for a precipitate fellow

parts.note: snow is a form of precipitation falling from clouds
a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A horse suitable for a hasty man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' suggests a horse; it is a mountain, the highest in Wales. 'precipitate' looks like an adjective for rash but works as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales, so a mount in the sense of a peak.

clue.text: Attempt to accommodate people producing ornamental stonework

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the word for people goes inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a race is a people or ethnic group

explanation.surface: Someone tries to house people while making decorative carvings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is the decorative interlaced stone ribs in the upper part of a Gothic window.

clue.text: A timetable boss with work in hand

parts.note: the boss of a timetable is jokingly its head, i.e. the head of the schedule

explanation.surface: A manager in charge of timetables has plenty of jobs to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with work in hand' sounds like being busy, but it means having done work in advance of when it was due.
explanation.definitionFit: Work in hand means work already done in advance, so one is early relative to the plan.

clue.text: Find that the record has finished

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished, as in 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the record has stopped playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to come upon or uncover something, much like locating it.

clue.text: Ideal fare for Ramadan

parts.note: Ramadan is the Muslim month of daytime fasting, so the joke is that the food suits those who are fasting, read as quick takeaway meals

explanation.surface: A suggestion for meals during the Muslim holy month.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick takeaway meals such as burgers are a style of eating; the pun links them to fasting.

clue.text: Without majority union leader gets terribly enraged

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so take the first letter of union
terribly means badly, so the letters of enraged are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trade-union boss becomes furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without majority' reads as lacking a voting majority but means not yet having come of age; 'terribly' rearranges ENRAGED into NDERAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Majority is the age of legal adulthood, so lacking it means being too young.

clue.text: One who advocates taking power

explanation.surface: A champion of a cause seizes power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is only a link; the second definition is mathematical, the index showing how many times a number is multiplied.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate or proponent promotes an idea; in maths an index number such as the 2 in x squared is called this.

clue.text: Order to act as artistic sponsors causes bewilderment

parts.note: 'be' as a command tells someone to act as something, as in 'be good'
the Muses were the Greek goddesses who inspired the arts

explanation.surface: A command to become patrons of the arts leaves people baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse is to puzzle or confuse someone.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well unwelcome in the auction room

explanation.surface: A layabout is not wanted at the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a scoundrel or rogue; literally a poor item offered for sale at an auction.

clue.text: Little lady with a large prayer-book

parts.note: miss is the title for a young girl or unmarried woman
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A girl carries a big book of prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the texts for celebrating Mass in the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Show respect to a lady, but no one's date

explanation.surface: Rising when a woman enters, but nobody turns up to meet you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link. The first sense is rising to one's feet; the second is failing to keep a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising to one's feet honours a woman entering; jilting someone by not arriving for a planned meeting is also this.

clue.text: Arranged to leave

explanation.surface: Plans are made to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: It can mean laid out or displayed, and also to begin a journey or depart.

clue.text: Seem to have found a soft fruit

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing softly
a pear is a common orchard fruit

explanation.surface: Someone appears to have come upon a ripe piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft fruit' looks like one phrase, such as a berry, but splits into P for soft and PEAR for fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to give the impression of being, much like looking.

clue.text: Diane's sweet, but may engender unease

parts.note: Di is short for Diane, plus the possessive S
a comfit is a sugar-coated sweet

explanation.surface: Diane's confectionery could make you uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: COMFIT is an old word for a sugared sweet, often a coated seed or nut.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit is to disconcert or embarrass, which unsettles someone.

clue.text: Intimidate old, eccentric weaver

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of weaver are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd old cloth-maker frightens people.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to subdue someone through awe or fear, cowing them.

clue.text: Not a tradesman employed in futile renovation

indicators.note: employed in means working inside, so the letters sit within the words futile renovation

explanation.surface: A workman is hired for a pointless refit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' is a loose link here; the answer runs across the end of 'futile' into 'renovation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays roof or floor tiles is a skilled manual worker.

clue.text: Discourage man from getting a cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Someone puts off a man from obtaining a cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cleaner' suggests a person who cleans, but it is a cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a washing agent such as soap powder or washing-up liquid.
